image.caption: Sir Keir Starmer (second left) attended a service of thanksgiving at Westminster Abbey on Sunday to commemorate the 84th anniversary of the Battle of Britain. The 112-day fight for control of Britain’s skies between July and October 1940 was the first decisive battle in history fought entirely in the air
The sun rises behind the Statue of Liberty and the skyline of Brooklyn in New York City
Pavli Fair has taken place in Kirklareli, Turkey, for the past 114 years. One of the country’s oldest fairs, it was established to ensure the unity and solidarity of the people of the region
Members of the English Civil War re-enactment group The Marquess of Winchester’s Regiment take part in a “skirmish” at Basing House in Hampshire

Vets hold Itapira, a young female jaguar that had its paws burnt during recent fires in the Pantanal region, as she receives treatment before she can be reintroduced back into the wild at the Nex No Extinction institute in Corumba de Goias, Brazil
The Lydham Manor loco, built in December 1950, on the Dartmouth Steam Railway with Goodrington Sands, Paignton in the background
The Liberal Democrat leader Ed Davey plays volleyball on the beach in Brighton with children and staff from the local carers centre
A misty sunrise at Corfe Castle in Dorset. The castle was built shortly after the Norman conquest of 1066
The yearly Jane Austen celebration parade in Bath is attended by hundreds of people in Regency costumes re-enacting the 19th-century world inhabited by the English novelist
Sika deer at Wareham Heath in Dorset. The animals were introduced to parks and estates in Britain from Asia in the 1850s. Many escaped to form the wild herd

A “caixer”, or horse rider, at the Sant Nicolau Festival in Es Mercadal, Spain, in which riders enter the main square of the town and pass among the people making the horses jump to the rhythm of the popular song known as jaleo
Lava runs down from Mount Merapi, the most active volcano on the Java island, as volcanic activity increases on the 2,968 meters (9,738 feet) tall Indonesian mountain
Residents rescue an elderly woman from rising flood waters in the Romanian village of Slobozia Conachi after Storm Boris hit, killing four people in the country

A staff member with Another Place to Live at a preview of I Followed You to the End, a new exhibition by the artist Tracey Emin at White Cube Bermondsey, south London. On display are paintings, one of her largest bronze sculptures, as well as the debut of a short film. The show runs from 19 September to 10 November

Dutch supporters of Extinction Rebellion block the A12 highway in the Netherlands, three days before the government presents its plans for the coming year on Budget Day, in the Hague. The climate action group is demanding that the government stop billions in tax breaks for the fossil industry immediately

image.caption: Shrink 01995 by Lawrence Malstaf is a performance artwork that was on display at the Great North Museum in Newcastle as part of NOVUM festival. The Newcastle resident Isadora Falstaff, 17, holds a pose between two large, transparent plastic sheets with a device that gradually sucks the air out from between them leaving her body vacuum-packed. The transparent tube inserted between the two surfaces allows her to regulate the flow of air

I was assigned to take photographs of the former chancellor Jeremy Hunt for an interview with The Sunday Times. We met at an outside dining area of a cafe in Godalming in his constituency just a few weeks after the general election. Jeremy is someone I have photographed many times, especially in the build up to the election, but I found him in a buoyant mood — the most upbeat I’d seen him in a long time

Anti-immigration protests and counter-protests took place in Leeds city centre after the Southport murders in July. The anti-immigration protesters marched around the city several times. There were a couple of arrests and some scuffles

An official at Hampton Court Palace directs a vintage 1962 AC Cobra to its parking place as it arrives in the grounds for the start of the Concours of Elegance, which is Europe’s leading “concours d’élégance” event, assembling dozens of the rarest privately owned cars from around the world

I arrived early in the morning for the Glorious Goodwood festival and, as I was wandering around the course, I came across the Goodwood shop where I found Victoria Gardiner preparing their display of the distinctive Panama hats worn as an essential fashion item by racegoers at the festival

Faith Sweeney, 9, helps Peter Rowell and John Shelley of the National Festival circus to ensure that their teeth are squeaky clean during a roaming performance at Thirsk Racecourse’s family fun day in North Yorkshire

I always try to take photographs away from the pomp and ceremony of the Sovereign’s Parade at Sandhurst military academy, so was happy to come across this group of graduating officer cadets wiping lint and dust from a fellow cadet’s uniform prior to the start of the parade

Photographing A-level students on their results day, I was somewhat distracted as I waited anxiously to hear the results of my own daughter. As I photographed the students celebrating my phone rang. It was my daughter, thankfully she had done very well. Shortly after that call I took this photograph of students at Lady Eleanor Holles school in Hampton, which mirrored what I was feeling inside
The dinosaur expert Jason Hyde, 5, gets to know Bruno the tyrannosaurus as the summer holidays draw to a close in Darlington town centre, Co Durham

I shadowed the consultant surgeon Paddy Subramanian as he prepared a patient for knee-replacement surgery at Chase Farm Hospital in Enfield, north London, where surgery is carried out in a “barn theatre” — a large operating theatre within the hospital that allows several operations to be carried out in the same room at the same time. The operating spaces are separated by large screens. It was fascinating to look across the room and see so many surgeries taking place at once. This type of multiple surgery is hoped to reduce the waiting time for patients

What photographer doesn’t like to photograph a steam locomotive? On a quiet news day in August I travelled down to the Bluebell Railway in Sussex where I found the volunteers there preparing Britain’s newest steam train, Beachy Head, for its first passenger service which was to start later in the week. Beachy Head is a full scale reproduction of a 1911 H2 Marsh Atlantic steam train and was built over a number of years by volunteers at the Bluebell line

Millie Kay, trainee valuer at Ryedale Auctioneers in Kirkbymoorside, poses with an eclectic collection of circus posters which are being sold on behalf of a circus technician who collected them over many years

Members of Extinction Rebellion created a camp in the Home Park in Windsor, under the gaze of Windsor Castle, where they were to hold a weekend of activism. It was a good humoured and well organised event. As I roamed around  taking photographs, two activists wearing King Charles and Queen Camilla masks walked through the camp on a mock royal visit. What better way to photograph the “royal couple” than in one of their tents!

The Monumentality of the Everyday by the artist Jakup Ferri is on show at the Harewood House Biennial at the Create/Elevate exhibition. Ferri’s inspiration comes from all kinds of otherworldly micro-organisms (bacteria, viruses, fungi, archaea) as seen through an electron microscope. It runs until October 20
Winfred Yavi looks back at devastated favourite Peruth Chemutai as she crosses the finish line in the women’s 3000 meter steeplechase final at the Stade de France.
Team GB’s injured cyclists: Jack Carlin on the left and Hamish Turnbull. Both of them crashed out of their races on the final day of racing in the Velodrome
The moment that Team GB’s Toby Roberts realised he had won gold in the men’s boulder and lead final
Uzbekistan’s Abdumalik Khalokov takes a blow on the nose from Spain’s Jose Quiles in the men’s 57kg quarterfinal boxing match. Khalokov won the bout
Keeley Hodgkinson, who won the women’s 800 metres, savours her gold medal
The moment that Team GB’s Christopher Jordan Houlden touched the water during the men’s 3m springboard final at the aquatics centre
Heartbreak for Team GB’s Joe Clarke who was one of the favourites in the canoeing slalom C-1 as he comes in fifth
A bit of fun with the skateboarder Andrew MacDonald who, at 51, is the oldest Olympic skateboarder
A scene from the closing ceremony, with the silhouettes of the competing athletes in the foreground

Lucas, 11, and Joseph Ashworth, 8, help to clean the engine of a 1909 steam traction engine called Dreadnought, belonging to Peter Turner. It arrived at Scampston Hall near Malton, North Yorkshire, for the Traction Engine Rally. The engine was used in the early 20th century to power showman’s fairground rides. It is road legal, with a top speed of 12mph
